text.0_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE JORDAN, IN THE LAND OF MOAB, MOSES UNDERTOOK TO EXPOUND.  Since they were no longer wandering, as the steppes of Moab was the camping place after the last leg of the journey.  Besides, after Moshe had pled his case and despaired of being able to cross, he undertook to clarify matters as to which he thought uncertainty might arise after his death.  He began his clarification by saying, later on (Deut. 5:2), "Adonai our God made a covenant with us at Horeb." AND HE SAID.  And before he began the clarification, in which he multiplied his admonitions regarding some of the mitzvot, he said to Israel that what necessitated this clarification and the admonitions now was that they were crossing into the Land without him, and he would not be able to admonish them when the need arose, nor to clarify any point of uncertainty that might arise.  And he recounted how they had failed in that he could not cross with them, through their poor choice and their sins, so that they would avoid this from here on and not ruin their affairs.
text.0_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: WE ENTERED THE GREAT AND TERRIBLE WILDERNESS.  Which no person had crossed, because of the many snakes and scorpions, and their size, as it says (Deut. 8:15), "[the wilderness of] snakes, serpents, and scorpions," and our Sages have already said that there were, there, snakes like beams and scorpions like bows.  And God, may He be blessed, did all this to shorten their way, so that they could enter the land immediately, "before the thorns grow into a bramble" (Ps. 58:10).  But all of this did not suffice, because in the mean time, they sinned with respect to the "complainers" (Num. 11:1), the "gluttonous craving" (id. 4), and ultimately the spies.
text.0_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) THEN ALL OF YOU CAME TO ME.  Even though you had chiefs appointed over you for public matters, all of you came.
text.0_Chapter, 21_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) LET US SEND AGENTS.  Let us, ourselves, choose persons and we will send them.  And to this, God, may He be exalted, did not agree, and He said to Moshe (Num. 13:2), "You send" -- that he, and not they, should send them, lest they choose common persons who would sin further.  And thus, Moshe chose ones who were (id. 3) "all men of consequence," and Yehoshua and Kalev among them.  And even the bad ones among them, though they sinned by saying that it was impossible to conquer [the land,] did not dare to say that the land was bad, and in fact sang its praises, such that afterward they repented, as he said (Deut. 1:41, 45), "You replied to me, saying, 'We stand guilty before Adonai,'" and "you repented and cried before Adonai."
text.2_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: YOUR MIGHTY HAND.  To alter the nature of the unchanging elements of the created world, which no one but You can do. You performed all of these deeds to bring Israel to the land, and therefore it is appropriate to secure their settlement there.
text.2_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) LET ME CROSS OVER. To eliminate all the residents of Canaan, so that Israel may never be exiled from it.
text.2_Chapter, 24_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND LET ME SEE THE GOOD LAND. Let me set my eyes on it as a positive force in my blessing, so that it will be good for Israel forever.
text.2_Chapter, 25_Verse, 0_Comment: ADONAI BECAME ANGRY WITH ME FOR YOUR SAKE [JPS: ON YOUR ACCOUNT].  Because I yearned to establish you in it so that you would never be exiled from it, but He had already sworn to scatter them.
text.3_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: DO NOT TAKE ANYTHING AWAY FROM IT, SO AS TO SAFEGUARD.  No person should think that, since the concerns underlying the mitzvah are no longer present for that person, eliminating the mitzvah would not be a violation, as King Solomon thought: "I will multiply [wives] and not go astray; I will multiply [horses] and not send back [to Egypt]," and he succumbed.
text.3_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: YOU HAVE SEEN WITH YOUR OWN EYES.  Look, evidence of this [of lesser violations leading to greater ones] is what you saw happen in connection with Ba'al Pe'or.  For indeed, those who sinned in worshiping Ba'al Pe'or did not initially intend to do that; rather, their initial intent was solely to fornicate, as it says (Num. 25:1), "the people began by whoring."  And even though the Torah forbade this out of concern [lest it lead to] idolatry, as they said (Ex. 34:16), "their daughters will lust [after their gods] and will cause your sons to lust [after their gods]."  Each one of them thought that this would not happen to him at all, and the opposite happened -- each one who went after Ba'al Pe'or to cleave to their daughters, there was not one of them who wisely refrained from succumbing to [idolatrous] worship itself, with the result that ADONAI YOUR GOD DESTROYED HIM.
text.3_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: BUT YOU WHO HELD FAST TO ADONAI YOUR GOD ARE ALL ALIVE TODAY.  You were all  wise enough to refrain from stumbling into the worship of Ba'al Peor.
text.3_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: FOR IT IS YOUR WISDOM.  It is through it that you can respond to a heretic with intellectual proofs.
text.3_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: FOR WHAT GREAT NATION IS THERE THAT HAS A GOD SO CLOSE AT HAND.  The reason why you should take pains to be considered wise and discerning by the nations is that God is close to us whenever we call to Him. And this shows that He chose us from among all the nations.  And if the  nations should come to consider you to be fools, it would be desecration of God when they say (Ezek. 36:20), "These, Adonai's people?"
text.3_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) TAKE UTMOST CARE.  Even though I have said that you should take pains to be considered wise by the nations, be careful to avoid the opinions of those who err in denying the existence, the power, or the oversight of God, may He be blessed.  And they thought to adduce intellectual arguments for all of this.  ...
text.3_Chapter, 8_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) LEST YOU FORGET THE THINGS THAT YOU SAW WITH YOUR OWN EYES.  The reason why I warned you strenuously to be careful about this is that you must take care to avoid forgetting what your physical eyes saw at Sinai, and your mental eyes [saw] likewise in interpreting the Torah, through which you were shown, through intellectual proofs, the opposite of their views.
text.3_Chapter, 8_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND MAKE THEM KNOWN TO YOUR CHILDREN. To your children who did not see at that time, you should inform them of these intellectual proofs.
text.6_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AND IT WILL BE BECAUSE YOU HEARKEN.  The King commanded all of these so that you will merit that He keep the covenant and the kindness.  And by your paying attention today to do them out of love, and not in order to receive a reward, so He, for the sake of this, will maintain the covenant and the lovingkindness for you.
text.6_Chapter, 11_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) THE RULES (MISHPATIM).  For (Prov. 29:4) "by justice (mishpat) [the king] sustains the land" [as applied here, it is primarily through observance of civil law that God will set out the Land for us].
text.6_Chapter, 11_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND YOU WILL TAKE CARE.  This is study (e.g., Sifrei 58).
text.6_Chapter, 11_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) TO DO THEM.  And in this manner, you will do them in the proper way.
text.6_Chapter, 11_Verse, 4_Comment: (5) THEN GOD WILL KEEP FOR YOU THE COVENANT that He swore, saying (Gen. 17:7), "I will maintain My covenant between Me and you, and your offspring to come, as an everlasting covenant throughout the ages, to be God to you and to your offspring to come."  For indeed, in His being God to us, without any intermediary, there will flow down permanent existence from Him without any intermediary, as it says (Eccl. 3:14), "whatever God has brought to pass will recur evermore:"  However, the existence of the transient ones is surely from Him but mediated.
text.6_Chapter, 11_Verse, 5_Comment: (6) AND THE KINDNESS.  As it says (Gen. 17:8), "I assign the land you sojourn in to you and your offspring to come."  For surely, the good that inures in this world to the righteous is kindness (hesed) alone, and not compensation for their good deeds.
text.6_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) [GOD] WILL LOVE YOU.  By virtue of your being children, in His likeness and His image, as [the Sages] said (Avot 3:14), "Beloved are [Israel] in that they are called children to the Omnipresent," and in this way the eternal nature of the covenant will be a happy one.
text.6_Chapter, 12_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND HE WILL BLESS YOU.  With wealth for the transitory life, and in this way, He will provide the hesed as when he swore that you would live on the land happily.
text.6_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) ALL SICKNESS.  Even those that customarily arise naturally.
text.6_Chapter, 14_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) ABOUT WHICH YOU KNOW.  That [the Egyptians] were smitten with at the Sea, as is explained above [on Exod. 14:24].
text.6_Chapter, 14_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) HE WILL NOT BRING THEM UPON YOU BUT WILL INFLICT THEM UPON ALL YOUR ENEMIES.  Even though He will inflict them on your ememies, they will not infect you, as in (Ps. 91:7), "A thousand may fall at your left side ... but it shall not reach you."
text.6_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) DO NOT SHOW THEM PITY AND DO NOT WORSHIP THEIR GODS.  Do not pity, and in this way you will not worship their gods, for if you pity, they will certainly cause you to sin.
text.6_Chapter, 15_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) FOR THAT WOULD BE A SNARE TO YOU.  For certainly your pitying them will be a snare for you, as they will seduce you to worship their gods.
text.6_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: HE WILL DELIVER THEIR KINGS  INTO YOUR HAND, AND YOU SHALL OBLITERATE THEIR NAME FROM UNDER THE HEAVENS.  For indeed, the persistence of your enemies' royal descendants will be an ongoing adversary against you, in the manner of Hadad, the young boy who was of the royal line of Edom and who arose to oppose Shlomo.
text.6_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: LEST YOU BE ENSNARED THEREBY.  For it may sometimes occur that you will succeed financially through the silver and gold that is on them [the idols], and you will attribute [the success] to the idol on which [the silver and gold] were.
text.6_Chapter, 25_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) ABOMINATE IT BECAUSE IT IS PROSCRIBED.  Abominate that silver and gold of the idol.
text.6_Chapter, 25_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) BECAUSE IT IS PROSCRIBED.  Not only will it occur that you will not succeed financially through it, but it will render your other possessions proscribed.
text.11_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: THESE ARE THE LAWS AND RULES THAT YOU MUST TAKE CARE ... TO POSSESS IT FOR ALL TIME.  And from among all these mitzvot, these are the ones that you must observe, through whose fulfillment you will acquire the Land for all time:  that you wipe out the sites of all idolatry and not do similar things for God, may He be blessed, that you not sacrifice to Him in every place whatsoever, but that you have a special site to sacrifice to Him, a site that Adonai your God will choose amidst all your tribes.
text.11_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) TO CAUSE HIM TO DWELL [JPS: TO HIS DWELLING PLACE].  For there to be there a tabernacle to His name, that being Shiloh or the Temple.
text.11_Chapter, 4_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) YOU SHALL SEEK.  To that chosen place you shall seek, as in (Isa. 11:10), "the nations shall seek that" [JPS: Nations shall seek His counsel].
text.11_Chapter, 4_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) THERE YOU ARE TO GO.  Not that the tabernacle of His name should come to you, like the practice of the idolaters.
text.11_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) BEFORE ADONAI YOUR GOD, AND YOU SHALL FEAST.  "Worship Adonai in gladness" (Ps. 100:2) as is appropriate for anyone who serves out of love.
text.11_Chapter, 6_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) IN ALL  YOUR UNDERTAKINGS.  For then you will succeed in all your ways and then you will prosper.
text.11_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AND YOU SAY, "I SHALL EAT SOME MEAT."  Without my having the burden of bringing it up to the Temple.
text.11_Chapter, 19_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) FOR YOU HAVE THE URGE TO EAT MEAT.  Also when you wish to eat that portion that is given to the priests from the sacrifice.
text.11_Chapter, 19_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) YOU MAY EAT MEAT WHENEVER YOU WISH.  But not the prohibited fat or blood even though they are non-sacrificial animals.
text.11_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: BUT MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT PARTAKE OF THE BLOOD.  Even though you hope that, by your eating it, the band of demons who tell you the future, as the Sages said (Hag. 16a) that [the demons] hear [from behind God's curtain] what will happen in the future, as the angels do, do not eat the blood in order to join with them.
text.11_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: YOU MUST NOT PARTAKE OF IT; YOU MUST POUR IT OUT ON THE GROUND LIKE WATER.  Act in a way that it will not be fit to eat, this being that you shall pour it on the ground like water, and do not put it aside as one puts aside wine, oil, and other liquids for eating and drinking.
text.11_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: DO NOT CONSUME IT ... BECAUSE YOU MUST DO WHAT IS RIGHT IN ADONAI'S EYES.  And when you refrain from consuming, let it not be like one who is disgusted by it, but rather in order to do what is right in Adonai's eyes.  As [the Sages] said, "Do not say, 'I have no desire for pig's meat,' but rather say, 'I do desire pig's meat, but my Father in heaven prohibited [it] to me.'"
text.13_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) YOU ARE CHILDREN OF ADONAI YOUR GOD. YOU SHALL NOT GASH YOURSELVES. It is not appropriate to display the extreme of worry and pain for a dead relative when there remains a more esteemed relative. Thus you are children of Adonai, for He is your Father, enduring forever, and it is not appropriate for you to worry and mourn in the extreme for any death. ...
text.13_Chapter, 0_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) NOR SHALL YOU SHAVE THE FRONT OF YOUR HEADS BECAUSE OF THE DEAD, FOR YOU ARE A PEOPLE CONSECRATED. Nor should one be very sorrowful for the injury experienced by the dead person in his death, for you are a holy people, destined for the life in the world to come, and the satisfaction in that life is better than all the life in this world.
text.15_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) MAGISTRATES AND OFFICIALS.  After the mitzvot for the multitudes, he commanded matters for their leaders, they being the judges [16:18 - 17:1], the kings [17:14-20], the priests [18:1-8], and the prophets [18:14-22], in whose perfection there would be perfected the affairs of the multitudes, and in whose corruption those affairs would be corrupted, as the prophet testified, in saying (Tz'fania 3:3-4), "The officials within her / Are roaring lions; / Her judges are wolves of the steppe, / They leave no bone until morning. / Her prophets are reckless, / Totally faithless; / Her priests profane what is holy, / They give perverse rulings."
text.15_Chapter, 17_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) IS GIVING YOU FOR YOUR TRIBES.  In your gates that He is giving you for you to apportion among the tribes, not in what you may conquer outside the Land, which will not be apportioned among the tribes, as they said (see Makkot 7a), Outside the Land, you do not establish judges in every district and every city.  And this is as in Syria and the like.
text.15_Chapter, 17_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) DUE JUSTICE.  Let the receiving of the complaints be such that they will render verdicts justly, and not be lenient on this one and harsh on that one.
text.15_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) JUSTICE, JUSTICE SHALL YOU PURSUE.  When you install judges -- you who appoint the judges -- choose the ones who are the most just, even if they do not have to the same degree other attributes desirable for a judge, like ample material resources and ample bodily stature, as with (I Sam. 16:7), "Pay no attention to his appearance or his stature."
text.15_Chapter, 19_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) SO THAT YOU MAY LIVE AND OCCUPY.  You will need this more in the Land, because the lack of it will interfere with the occupying of the Land, as he said (Isa. 57:17), "For their sinful greed I was angry."
text.16_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) IF THERE IS FOUND AMONG YOU.  After he commanded to appoint judges in each city, for each court to adjudicate for the residents of its city, he mentions the case of the idolater, who is not tried in his city, but rather in the city where he committed the idolatry.  And after that, he mentions the matter of a disagreement between two courts, since that is also adjudicated in another city, that being "the place that Adonai shall choose" (v.8), and similarly the matter of the rebellious elder.
text.16_Chapter, 1_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) TRANSGRESSING THE COVENANT.  The covenant that covers all of the commandments, for indeed, the idolater is denying all of the commandments and nullifying them.
text.16_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) OTHER GODS.  Supernal beings aside from God, may He be blessed.
text.16_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND TO THE SUN OR THE MOON.  Which are material.
text.16_Chapter, 2_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) WHICH I DID NOT DESIGNATE (JPS: SOMETHING I NEVER COMMANDED).  To which I did not assign any function of choosing, such that they could act in furtherance of their will.  Rather, I gave them strict [physical] laws, which they could not transgress.  This is the opposite of what the idolaters think, that each city has its tutelary spirit, which can, as it wishes, provide benefit or harm, and that it provides benefits if one worships it.
text.16_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) EITHER THAT MAN OR THAT WOMAN.  And we do not say that [a woman's violation] was due to being seduced/misled, so it's not necessary to try her in the place where the act occurred in order to teach that her mindset was wrong.
text.16_Chapter, 4_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) TO YOUR GATES.  To the gate [i.e., the city] where he committed the idolatry, so as to make manifest that the deity that he worshiped would not save him.
text.16_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: IF A CASE IS TOO BAFFLING FOR YOU.  Even though you have appointed judges in each city, so that each court can adjudicate for its city, when there arises a doubt as to what is the authentic tradition with respect to a particular question, the local court should not adjudicate the matter according to their view; rather, the ruling should be according to the assessment of a majority of the Supreme Court.  Similarly when there is no majority [in the local court].
text.16_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: ONE WHO ACTS PRESUMPTUOUSLY [JPS:  SHOULD THE [LOSING] PARTY ACT PRESUMPTUOUSLY].  Who makes a practical halachic ruling contrary to the pronouncement of the Supreme Court, THAT PERSON SHALL DIE according to the decision of the Supreme Court, so that the people will hear and be deterred.
text.16_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: I WILL SET A KING OVER ME, AS DO ALL THE NATIONS.  Such that the kingship will be his and his descendants'.  This is unlike the Judges, for a Judge would reign he alone, but not his descendants after him. And regarding the appointment of a Judge to be king in this fashion on their entry into the Land, they were commanded, as it says (Num. 27:17), "so that Adonai's community may not be like sheep that have no shepherd."  Indeed, that he should be like the kings of the nations, with the kingship held by him and his descendants, is repugnant to God, may He be blessed, but He commanded that when they would stiffen their neck to set over themselves a king in this fashion, they should choose only a fit person whom Adonai would select (v.15), and who would not cause Israel to transgress the religion, and who would not be a foreigner (v.15), even if he was a fit person, and even if he was mighty and a warrior. And when they sinned by requesting a king who would rule, both he and his descendants, as with the other nations, their punishment was the disasters that befell the multitudes on account of the king, as it says (I Sam. 8:18), "The day will come when you cry out because of the king whom you yourselves have chosen; and Adonai will not answer you on that day," and as it says (Hos. 13:11), "I give you kings in My ire, And take them away in My wrath."  The permission to appoint a king was like the permission to take the beautiful woman [battle captive as a wife], as to which [the Torah] hinted that [the man] would ultimately hate her and beget from her a stubborn and rebellious son, as happened to David in connection with Avshalom.
text.16_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: SO THAT HE WILL STUDY, IN ORDER TO REVERE.  [He will study] the contemplative portion of it, which shows through example the greatness and oversight of God, may He be exalted, since from knowledge of this, reverence is compelled.
text.20_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: HE MAY NOT TREAT AS FIRST-BORN THE SON OF THE LOVED ONE IN DISREGARD OF THE SON OF THE UNLOVED ONE WHO IS THE OLDER.  He may not transfer the birthright because of this dislike or this love, but if he does so based on the bad character of the first-born, then it is appropriate to transfer [it], as they said, "[If a person gives his estate, in writing, to strangers, and leaves out his children, his arrangements are legally valid,  but the spirit of the sages finds no delight in him.  R. Shime'on b. Gamliel said,] If his children did not conduct themselves in a proper manner he will be remembered for good."  And it seems that Ya'akov our patriarch acted similarly, as it says (I Chron. 5:1), "but when he [Re'uven] defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel."
text.20_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: WAYWARD AND DEFIANT.  For his defiance turns away [mesir] the hope that he will repent of his waywardness [sor'rato].
text.20_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: A GLUTTON AND A DRUNKARD.  For a drunkard and a glutton will become impoverished and will turn to brigandage to satisfy his spirit.
text.20_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AN IMPALEMENT IS A CONTEMPT TO GOD.  Now every being that is divorced from material existence is called "Elohim."  And within this category is the being that is the intellectual soul in a human, which is called (Gen. 1:27) "the image of God."  And it was in this manner that the witch spoke to Shmu'el, saying (I Sam. 28:13), "I see a divine being coming up."  And since the shame that is inflicted on a dead person after death is a shaming of the intellectual spirit, which is a separated being that remains after the death of the body, it says that this is a contempt of, or a curse against, "elohim," because leaving the body of the dead impaled person overnight, without burial, is a disgrace to that eternal being that is called "elohim."
text.20_Chapter, 22_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) DO NOT DEFILE.  To cause the spirit of impurity in the place of the rotting unburied dead.
text.21_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: THAT YOU MAY FARE WELL AND HAVE A LONG LIFE.  With regard to the sending from the nest, there is some amount of "deeds of lovingkindness" for the multitudes, in not destroying the descendants of field birds, which are ownerless.  And this [is effected by] sending the mother.  It says that even through this slight bit of deeds of lovingkindness, there will be "consuming the interest in this world and the principal in the world to come."
text.21_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: IF A MAN TAKES A WIFE.  After the statement relating to settlement [of the Land], it states prohibitions [whose observance] will compel the resting of the Divine Presence on Israel and [it commands] refraining from causing removal [of the Presence] through the disqualification of the line, on account of sexual sins, or on account of mingling with ineligible nations, or on account of unseemliness in your camp, as it says (Deut. 23:15), "let your camp be holy; let [God] not find anything unseemly among you and turn away from you."
text.21_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) BECAUSE HE IMPOVERISHED HIS FELLOW'S WIFE [JPS: BECAUSE HE VIOLATED HIS NEIGHBOR’S WIFE].  He made her poorer and reduced her from her fit status, and disqualified her from being permitted to his fellow her husband, as in (Micah 2:9), "You drive the women of My people away From their homes of pleasure."
text.21_Chapter, 25_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) THE YOUNG WOMAN DID NOT INCUR THE DEATH PENALTY.  Even though she was participating willingly at the end, since she was compelled at the beginning, she is exempt, since once she began in the prohibition, her desire overpowered her, as (the Sages) said (Ket. 51b), "even if she said, 'Leave him alone', etc."
text.21_Chapter, 25_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) FOR THIS CASE IS LIKE THAT OF ONE PARTY ATTACKING ANOTHER, ETC.  This is unlike the case of a man having sexual relations with an animal, about which it is written (Lev. 20:15), "you shall kill the animal," for indeed, the animal did not resist at all, but this woman, whose intercourse began by being compelled, and she resisted as much as she could, what happened to her is like what happened to a murder victim, against whom a violation was committed against his will.  Therefore, she has no guilt at all.
text.21_Chapter, 26_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) THE WOMAN CRIED FOR HELP.  We give her the benefit of the doubt.
text.25_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: SOME OF THE BEST OF ALL THE FRUITS [JPS:  SOME OF EVERY FIRST FRUIT] OF THE SOIL WHICH YOU HARVEST FROM THE LAND.  The choicest of all its fruits, as in (Amos 6:6), "they anoint themselves with the choicest [reishit] oils," [and] (Amos 6:1), "notables of the leading [reishit] nations."  The "choicest" are the seven species with which the Land of Israel is distinguished, as we have from tradition.  This is the explanation of what is commanded above when it says (Ex. 23:19), "The choice first fruits of your soil you shall bring."  And it makes clear that in saying "The choice first fruits of your soil," the intent was that you should bring the first fruits from the choicest fruits of your soil, and those are the seven species with which it is distinguished.
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) TO THE PRIEST WHO WILL  BE IN THOSE DAYS.  Even if he is not very wise, do not desist from speaking with him respectfully, saying "Adonai your God," even though this is said only to persons of renown, as to kings and to prophets.  Nevertheless, when you bring him the first fruits, like bringing a tribute to God, may He be exalted, for He is the owner of the soil, it is appropriate to speak with him respectfully,
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) I HAVE DECLARED [JPS:  I ACKNOWLEDGE] THIS DAY.  I have declared to everyone with this act of mine, as with (II Sam. 19:7), "For you have made clear today that the officers and servicemen mean nothing to you."
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) THAT I HAVE ENTERED THE LAND. That I have come from another land to this land.
text.25_Chapter, 2_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) THAT ADONAI SWORE TO OUR FATHERS TO ASSIGN US.  As it says (Gen. 17:8), "I have given to you and your offspring to come."  Therefore, I, the stranger, who have come to the land as a resident by way of [Divine] gift, have brought the first fruits to the One who gave the land as a gift or as a sharecropping arrangement.
text.25_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: HE SHALL SET IT DOWN IN FRONT OF THE ALTAR OF ADONAI YOUR GOD.  To show and to proclaim that the first fruits were not brought to the priest, but were brought to God, may He be blessed, and He gave them to the priest with the other gifts to the priests.
text.25_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: HE GAVE US THIS LAND.  And after we had emerged into freedom, we had no portion in the earth on which to settle, and He gave us this, which is A LAND that is chosen, OOZING MILK AND HONEY.
text.25_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) NOW (JPS: WHEREFORE).  Since I realize how great is Your goodness and kindness toward us, that You have made us a nation fit to own land, and to bring us out into freedom so that we can receive the gift that will be ours, and You have given us this, which is more splendid than all lands and the choicest of places, --
text.25_Chapter, 9_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) I HAVE BROUGHT THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SOIL WHICH YOU HAVE GIVEN ME, ADONAI.   I have brought the choicest fruits of that land that You have given me, to give thanks to Your name for it.
text.25_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) I HAVE CLEARED OUT THE CONSECRATED PORTION FROM THE HOUSE.  Through our sins and the transgressions of our ancestors, the service was removed from the first-born, to whom the elevation offerings and tithes had been due, as it says (Ezek. 20:26), "I defiled them from their gifts by sidelining every first issue of the womb."  And this is the "Confession of the Tithe" to which our Rabbis referred.
text.25_Chapter, 12_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND HAVE ALSO GIVEN IT TO THE LEVITE. The meaning of "gam" is like "even though," as in (Ruth 1:12), "even if I were married tonight and even if I bore sons."  Thus, he is to say, "I acknowledge that my sin is great, such that I have caused the removal of the holy things from the house.  And even though I have given it to the Levite and his like, according to your commandment, I pray that You gaze with a favorable gaze, instead of the unfavorable gaze that would be appropriate, given my sin."
text.25_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: BLESS YOUR PEOPLE ... AND THE LAND YOU HAVE GIVEN US in the same manner that YOU SWORE TO OUR FATHERS, when You said, "I will take you out of the misery of Egypt to a good and spacious land, etc." (see Exod. 3:8, 17).
text.28_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) YOU ARE STANDING before Adonai your God, and anyone who can deceive me will not be able to deceive Him, and it is on His knowledge that you will accept obligations on yourselves, --
text.28_Chapter, 8_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) YOUR CHIEFS -- YOUR RULERS -- [JPS: TRIBAL HEADS], YOUR ELDERS, AND YOUR OFFICIALS.  Your chiefs, who are your rulers [your sh'vatim] -- the staffs [sh'vatim] of your governors, and they are the princes and the officials who have in their hands the staff of a governor.
text.28_Chapter, 8_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) YOUR ELDERS.  They are the judges.
text.28_Chapter, 8_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) YOUR OFFICIALS.  Who have the power to compel litigants.  And the responsibility rests on all of these chiefs to instruct the multitudes as to what is good for them to accept on themselves or to eschew.
text.28_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) YOUR CHILDREN, YOUR WIVES.  Whose actions should be done with the assent of the fathers and the husbands.
text.28_Chapter, 9_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) FROM THE WOODCHOPPER TO THE WATER-DRAWER.  From the first among the woodchoppers to the last among the water-drawers, as in (I Sam. 15:3), "from infant to suckling, from ox to sheep, from  camel to donkey."
text.28_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) FOR YOUR CROSSING [JPS: TO ENTER] INTO THE COVENANT.  You are standing, with this whole list and [the ones mentioned based on] the assent, prepared to be crossing into the covenant, and from this one can see that all of you are desirous of accepting [it] on you wholeheartedly.
text.28_Chapter, 10_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) WHICH ADONAI YOUR GOD IS CONCLUDING WITH YOU THIS DAY, IN ORDER TO ESTABLISH YOU ETC.  God, may He be blessed, intends by means of this covenant to establish you to Himself as a people, so that He will be as a God to you, and in this way, you will acquire everlasting life.  And since the purpose of this covenant is so glorious, its acceptance must be with the ultimate in wholeheartedness.
text.28_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: SINCE [JPS: WELL] YOU KNOW THAT WE DWELT.  And thus it is appropriate to take care.
text.28_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) PERHAPS THERE IS AMONG YOU SOME MAN OR WOMAN.  Perhaps their minds be seduced to the abominations of the nations [var.: Moabites] from your dwelling with them, and they think to annul acceptance of the covenant in their minds.  That is why I said that all of you are standing before Adonai, Who probes the feelings and the minds; you cannot deceive Him.
text.28_Chapter, 16_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) LEST THERE BE AMONG YOU A STOCK SPROUTING POISON WEED AND WORMWOOD.  Who plans to divert the multitudes to his false ideas.
text.28_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) HE ASSURES HIMSELF MENTALLY.  He accepts the oath orally, but in his mind, he assures himself benefits by nullifying it.
text.28_Chapter, 17_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) TO ADD THE MOIST TO THE DRY [JPS:  TO THE UTTER RUIN OF MOIST AND DRY].  The reason he accepts the oath orally is to add his sated self, satisfied with all his desires, to God's community, parched and separated from material desires, so as to rejoice with them in their blessings.
text.28_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: SULFUR AND SALT ... LIKE THE UPHEAVAL OF SODOM ... WHICH GOD OVERTHREW.  They would recognize that this was not happenstance, but rather the finger of God, for plainly, He did here just as He did with S'dom, for it was known that He had overthrown it.
text.28_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: ALL THE NATIONS WILL ASK.  When they [the Israelites] are exiled among them.
text.28_Chapter, 24_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) GODS WHOM THEY HAD NOT EXPERIENCED.  They did not know at all of their existence, and they abandoned their God, Who is the true God, though wonders establish His existence, His power, and His oversight.
text.28_Chapter, 24_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND WHO HAD NOT BEEN ALLOTTED TO THEM.  So that they would see that there is no constellation that orders their affairs.
text.28_Chapter, 27_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) CONCEALED ACTS CONCERN THE ETERNAL OUR GOD.  Even though I said (v.9) that "You stand ... all of you, before Adonai your God," Whom no one can deceive, and Who will punish the traitor, that applies to the hidden things alone.
text.28_Chapter, 27_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) BUT WITH OVERT ACTS, IT IS FOR US AND OUR CHILDREN FOREVER.  But as to the overt things, the matter rests on us and our children, and it is appropriate for us TO APPLY ALL THE PROVISIONS OF THIS TEACHING to punish the sinners and to carry out the prescribed laws regarding them.
text.30_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: MOSHE WENT.  He aroused himself for this, as in (Exod. 2:1), "A man from the House of Levi went,"  or (Deut. 17:3), "he went and worshiped," and the like.  And this -- that after he finished with matters of making the covenant, he aroused himself to comfort Israel regarding his death -- so that it [the news about his death] would not be mixed with the joy of the covenant, which it was appropriate for them to manifest upon their receiving the covenant with joy, in the manner of  (Ps. 149:2), "Let Israel rejoice in its Maker," as it says (Deut. 27:7), "you shall sacrifice there offerings of well-being and eat them, rejoicing before your God."
text.30_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) I AM 120 YEARS OLD TODAY.  And there is no need to be sad about my death, as I was not meant by nature to live longer.
text.30_Chapter, 1_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) I CAN NO LONGER BE ACTIVE.  And also, even if I were to live, I could not come and go in front of you in my old age.
text.30_Chapter, 1_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND ADONAI SAID TO ME, "YOU SHALL NOT CROSS."  And also, even if I could come and go, Adonai said to me, "You shall not cross," and if so, better for you that I die, so that you can cross.
text.30_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) ADONAI YOUR GOD IS THE ONE WHO WILL CROSS BEFORE YOU.  And so you need not be sad that you will lose my leadership, for in fact, Adonai your God is crossing before you, and thus, you will obtain leadership better than my leadership.
text.30_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) YEHOSHUA IS THE ONE WHO SHALL CROSS BEFORE YOU, AS ADONAI HAS SAID.  For, while Yehoshua is not the leader, he will cross before you at the instruction of God, may He be exalted, for He is the leader.
text.30_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) HE WILL NOT FAIL YOU.  For He will strengthen your hand in time of war.
text.30_Chapter, 5_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) OR FORSAKE YOU.  Afterward, He will not diminish His watchful providence, so that those around you will not rise up.
text.30_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: FOR YOU WILL GO.  Even though I have not merited to do so.
text.30_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) THIS TEACHING.  The section of the king [see M.Sotah 7:8], which He now commands should be read in plenary gathering.
text.30_Chapter, 8_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND HE GAVE IT TO THE PRIESTS, THE SONS OF LEVI.  For the king who reads it will receive it from their hands, as we have learned, "The Deputy gives it to the High Priest, and the High Priest to the king."
text.30_Chapter, 8_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) WHO BEAR THE ARK.  Who carried [it] at the time of the renewal of the miracle concerning it.
text.30_Chapter, 8_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) AND TO ALL THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL.  From whom the priests would receive the Torah at the time of the plenary gathering, as we have learned, "The hazzan of the assembly gives it to the head of the assembly, and the head of the assembly to the Deputy."
text.31_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) MAY MY DISCOURSE COME DOWN AS THE RAIN.  My Torah will come down and come in a flood like rain to the discerning ones who are prepared to receive the expression of the source of wisdom.
text.31_Chapter, 1_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) MY SPEECH DISTILL AS THE DEW.  And provides, according to what is revealed in it, some awareness to the common ones, which, though it be small, it is very good like dew; such that it [the Torah] is LIKE SHOWERS ON VERDURE [JPS: YOUNG GROWTH], that the enlightened ones will perceive wonders in it, ...
text.31_Chapter, 1_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND LIKE DROPLETS ON THE GRASS.  For the common ones also will acquire some knowledge to recognize their Creator in some way.  If so, you, Israel, who have accepted it [the Torah], [I now say:]--
text.31_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) FOR THE NAME OF ADONAI I PROCLAIM.   Here, the one who calls the name of Adonai is the one who prays, as it is said (Lam. 3:55), "I have called on Your name, O LORD, From the depths of the Pit," and similarly (Ps. 99:6), "and Shmu'el among those who call on His name— when they called to Adonai, He answered them."  He [Moshe] said, "If so, then when I pray for the ingathering of exiles, when I say (v.11), 'Like an eagle who rouses its nestlings, [Gliding down to its young, So did [God] spread wings and take them, Bear them along on pinions],' and for the coming of the Messiah, when I say (v.12), 'Adonai alone did guide them,' and at the end of the poem, when I say (v.43), 'O nations, acclaim God’s people,' you, who know the intellectual wonders made clear in His Torah, --
text.31_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) GIVE GLORY TO OUR GOD.  Do not attribute to Him mutability regarding what is recounted in the poem about Israel's future and that He would become like an enemy to you, for you know, through the wonders in His Torah, that He is --"
text.31_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) THE ROCK.  Unchanging.  His hand is not too short to save, His ear not too dull to hear.  (See Isa. 59:1). And also, do not attribute to Him any injustice, since you know through wonders that HIS WORK IS PERFECT in actuality -- nothing is to be added to it and nothing subtracted.
text.31_Chapter, 3_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) And through this it is known that ALL HIS WAYS ARE JUST.  The His ways of goodness and His attribute of justice are all undoubtedly just.
text.31_Chapter, 3_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) A FAITHFUL GOD.  Reliable in what He swore to the Patriarchs to do good to their children because of the merits of the ancestors.
text.31_Chapter, 3_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) NEVER UNJUST [JPS: FALSE].  In His bringing retribution.
text.31_Chapter, 3_Verse, 4_Comment: (5) RIGHTEOUS [JPS: TRUE].  "He loves righteous deeds" (Ps. 11:7), and in His righteousness, He will not forsake His people.
text.31_Chapter, 3_Verse, 5_Comment: (6) AND UPRIGHT INDEED.  He will not deprive any person of a reward, and will compensate His enemies [for their good deeds] openly, and therefore, He is patient and beneficent with the nations in this world.
text.31_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: THEY HAVE DESTROYED FOR HIM, HIS NON-CHILDREN, [BY] THEIR BASENESS, THE CROOKED AND PERVERSE GENERATION.  [JPS:  UNWORTHY CHILDREN— THAT CROOKED, PERVERSE GENERATION— THEIR BASENESS HAS PLAYED GOD FALSE].  However, the crooked and perverse generation are not His children in purity; their baseness in connection with the Calf has destroyed for God, may He be exalted, what was intended, as it is said (Exod. 32:7), "for your people have acted basely."  For He in fact had intended to sanctify Israel, and to sanctify His name in His world through them, so that they would be luminaries among humankind, to understand and to teach, as it is said (Exod. 19:5-6), "Indeed, all the earth is Mine, but you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests."  But they destroyed all this through the Calf.
text.31_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) DO YOU THUS REQUITE ADONAI?  Since He had intended to place you above all the nations, is it appropriate that you should requite Him this way, that you should frustrate His intent, that you should desecrate His holy name, and that you should prevent His achieving the end that He had planned in His saying (Gen. 1:25), "Let Us make humanity in Our image, after Our likeness"?
text.31_Chapter, 5_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) DULL PEOPLE.  Disgraced, through your owing gratitude, and repaying favors with evil, the opposite of the generous One, Who is honored in His doing good to one who has never done good for Him.
text.31_Chapter, 5_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND WITLESS.  In practical affairs, to understand the consequences of a matter, and what will be achieved.
text.31_Chapter, 5_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) IS NOT THIS THE FATHER WHO ACQUIRED [JPS: CREATED] YOU?  Not a natural father, who gives some measure of existence by chance; but He is an intentional father, Who gave you existence so that you would be His possession, prepared [for Him] to achieve His desire through you [and to make you] His treasure.  And this is because HE FASHIONED YOU into a nation, for you had not been a nation of any account at all.
text.31_Chapter, 5_Verse, 4_Comment: (5) AND PREPARED YOU [JPS: MADE YOU ENDURE].  He gave you preparations so that you would be prepared to be a treasured nation to Him.
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) REMEMBER THE DAYS OF OLD.  After he finished the introduction to the poem, in which he announced that the intent [of the poem] was to declare the righteousness of God, may He be blessed, Who is a faithful God, benefiting those who do His will and Who, having blessed, does not retract it, and there is no distortion in the quality of His judgment against them, Moshe begins to clarify this (Deut. 1:5) through telling the past and the future, to inform them:
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 1_Comment: First, of how much God, may He be blessed, sought to achieve this end for all of humanity in "the days of old" and "the years of ages past."  And how, when that did not come to pass, He did great things for them (Ps. 126:2-3), elevating Israel to the top rank (II Kings 9:13), as He will do at the end of days, with the remnant whom He will call (Joel 3:5).
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 2_Comment: Second, that He gave them a solid place to worship Him "in joy and gladness over the abundance of everything" (Deut. 28:47).  But they rebelled, and returned evil for good.  And whoever diverted His intent regarding all this, doubtless deserves significant punishment.
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 3_Comment: Third, that through the magnitude of their sins, they will fall into the snares of evil ones (see Ps. 141:10), and they deserved to be wiped out, but for the desecration of [God's] name [that would have resulted from their destruction], which prevented this.
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 4_Comment: Fourth, he announces the factor because of which there will be a redemption in the end of days.
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 5_Comment: Fifth, he announces the manner of the redemption, and God's compassion on the remnant of His people.
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 6_Comment: And these are the sections of Parashat Ha'azinu that the Sages mentioned and gave them the mnemonic HaZYU LaCH. He said, if so, "Remember the days of old" and contemplate the ways of His goodness and how much He intended to benefit humankind in general.  When you remember, first, how He benefited Adam at the beginning of the "days of old" and placed him in the Garden of Eden, but he ruined things.
text.31_Chapter, 6_Verse, 7_Comment: (2) CONSIDER THE YEARS OF AGES PAST.  And contemplate, second, how He benefited the [subsequent] generations, but they acted corruptly until the Flood, and similarly, third, from the Flood until the Dispersion, they caused ruin.
text.31_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) HE FIXED THE BOUNDARIES OF PEOPLES.  He set up boundaries for peoples at the time of the Dispersion, and He did not destroy them completely as they deserved.
text.31_Chapter, 7_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) IN RELATION TO ISRAEL’S NUMBERS.  For the sake of the Israelites, who would be few in number and would in the future emerge from  those peoples.
text.31_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) FOR ADONAI’S PORTION IS HIS PEOPLE.  For God, may He be blessed, has no other portion in humankind than His people.  For all the other nations are children of a foreign god.  And thus it is made clear that, were it not for His people, which would in the future emerge from those other nations, He should have destroyed them in the matter of the Dispersion.
text.31_Chapter, 8_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) YA'AKOV, HIS OWN ALLOTMENT.  For he and his children were servants to God, may He be exalted, but with the nations of the world, if there be found among them a saint, that would not extend to his children.
text.31_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) [GOD] FOUND THEM IN THE LAND OF THE WILDERNESS.  He found the mind of His people, who were His portion, faithful before Him in the wilderness, as it says (Jer. 2:2), "your following Me into the wilderness."
text.31_Chapter, 9_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) HE ENGIRDED THEM [LIT., IT],  Mt. Sinai, as it says (Exod. 19:12), "You shall set bounds for the people round about."
text.31_Chapter, 9_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) HE GAVE THEM UNDERSTANDING [JPS: WATCHED OVER THEM].  As it says (Exod. 24;12), "the instruction and the commandment that I have written to instruct them."
text.31_Chapter, 9_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) HE GUARDED THEM.  From the Egyptian enslavement and from the Angel of Death, as the Sages said, "'engraved [harut] on the tablets' -- free [herut] from the Angel of Death and from subjugation to the nations.
text.31_Chapter, 9_Verse, 4_Comment: (5) AS THE PUPIL OF ONE’S EYE.  As He protected the pupil of a person's eye when He created him -- He surrounded the eye with garments of leather so that it would not be lost, though it was susceptible to that.
text.31_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) LIKE AN EAGLE WHO ROUSES ITS NESTLINGS.  May it be [God's] will that, as He planned to do at Sinai, had they not sinned with the Calf, He will do in the future, and God, may He be blessed, will grant his prayer then, as it says (Zech. 10:8), "I will whistle to them and gather them, For I will redeem them.
text.31_Chapter, 10_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) GLIDING DOWN TO ITS YOUNG. As it says (Isa. 49:22), "I will raise My hand to nations And lift up My ensign to peoples; And they shall bring your sons in their bosoms."
text.31_Chapter, 10_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) SO DID [GOD] SPREAD WINGS AND TAKE THEM.  As it says (Isa. 27:12), "and you shall be picked up one by one, O children of Israel."
text.31_Chapter, 10_Verse, 3_Comment: (4) BEAR THEM ALONG ON PINIONS.  As it says (Isa. 60:8), "Who are these that float like a cloud?"
text.32_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: THIS IS THE BLESSING WITH WHICH MOSES [BLESSED ISRAEL (JPS: BADE THE ISRAELITES FAREWELL)].  When God, may He be blessed, showed him the whole Land before his death, so that he would bless the Land, and Israel in it, as had been his intent, when he said (Deut. 3:25), "Let me cross over and let me see," and as had been God's intent, may He be blessed, when He said to him (Num. 27:12), "and view the Land," -- this is the blessing that he blessed.
text.32_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) HE SAID.  Before he began the blessing, which begins (v.25), "May your doorbolts be iron and copper," he spoke this introduction, and prayed for the tribes, that his blessing might rest [on them], for certainly, the words of the blessing everywhere speak with the one who is blessed, as He said (Num. 6:23), "Speak to them," and so all of his words, from "iron and copper" to (v.29), "you shall tread on their backs," were with Israel, but the prior words were with God, requesting with respect to His people.
text.32_Chapter, 1_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) CAME FROM SINAI, AND SHONE ... LIGHTNING FLASHING AT THEM.  He mentions Israel's merits, so that his prayer for them would be accepted and his blessing would rest [on them], and he said to God, may He be blessed, "Hey, there came from Sinai, and shone, and appeared from various places to Israel the holy of flashing lightning, it being the inquiring part that comes from the multitudinous holy, from the right-hand side of the holy, for He indeed gave it transparently.
text.32_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) EVEN THOUGH [JPS: INDEED] [YOU ARE] A LOVER OF NATIONS [JPS: OF THE PEOPLE].  Even though You are a lover of nations, as You said (Exod. 19:5),, "you shall be My treasured possession more than [JPS: among] all the peoples," and in this way, You have made known that all of humankind is treasured by You, as they said (Avot 3:18), "The human is dear in that he was created in the image."  Nevertheless, ALL OF ITS [JPS: THEIR] HOLY ONES ARE IN YOUR HAND.  Here, You have said that all the ones sanctified by the holy of the fire-law are in Your hand like a bundle of coins, for they are dearer than the rest of the species, as He said (Exod. 19:6), "you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation," as they said (Avot 3:18), "Dear is Israel, in that they are called the children of the Omnipresent.
text.32_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) THEY FOLLOWED.  They were broken, as (Prov. 29:13) "and an oppressor" [NJPS: "a fraudulent man"].  They prayed with a broken spirit.
text.32_Chapter, 2_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) YOUR FEET [JPS: STEPS].  To your footstool on Sinai.
text.32_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) [v.23]  HE WILL LIFT UP YOUR STATEMENTS, THE TORAH THAT MOSHE COMMANDED US. [JPS: ACCEPTING YOUR PRONOUNCEMENTS.  MOSHE CHARGED US WITH THE TORAH.]  They said to God, may He be blessed, "Let Moshe bring us Your statements, which are the Torah that he commanded us, saying your statements, as it says (Num. 7:89). "he heard the voice speaking with him."
text.32_Chapter, 3_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) INHERITANCE OF THE CONGREGATION OF YA'AKOV.  [And] which is for an inheritance for the congregation of Ya'akov, accepted for us and as an inheritance for our children.
text.32_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AND IT HAPPENED THAT THE KING OF YESHURUN.  And then, the One who was King in Yeshurun, i.e., God, may He be blessed, Who was King for the inquiring ones and those who grasped the Torah,
text.32_Chapter, 4_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) UPON THE GATHERING OF THE HEADS OF THE PEOPLE. At the Giving of the Torah, as he said (Deut. 5:20), "you came up to me, all your tribal heads and elders," and he said (5:21), "[and you said,] 'Adonai our God has just shown us His presence, etc.'"
text.32_Chapter, 4_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL TOGETHER.  He was King over all the tribes of Israel together, for then they acknowledged and accepted His kingship, as they said (5:24), "then you tell us everything that Adonai our God tells you, and we will willingly do it."
text.32_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: (1)  MAY REUVEN LIVE.  Even though Reuven selected Transjordan, which is not part of God's land, as he [Yehoshua] said (Josh. 22:19), "If it is because the land of your holding is impure," and accordingly, it is not so fit for attaining through it eternal life, may he nevertheless thrive alone forever.
text.32_Chapter, 5_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND NOT DIE, THOUGH FEW BE HIS NUMBERS.  And not die in this world, in the manner that his population be few, as in (Gen. 34:30), "my fighters are few in number," even though it is written (Deut. 11:21), "to the end that you may endure in the land."
text.32_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AND THIS OF JUDAH.  And this request I also request and pray for the land of Yehudah, within which the allotment of Shimon is scattered, so that they will not die in war, for they would go out to war together.
text.32_Chapter, 6_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) HE SAID, HEAR, ADONAI, THE VOICE OF JUDAH.  In addition to what he said above -- "This of Yehudah" -- he also said, "Hear, Adonai, the voice of Yehudah" when he prays in war or outside of it.
text.32_Chapter, 6_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) THOUGH HIS OWN HANDS STRIVE FOR HIM,  HELP HIM AGAINST HIS FOES. You [God] be "his hands," fighting for him, and also be striving on his behalf and taking vengeance for him, and a help against his foes when they wage war against him.
text.32_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) LET YOUR THUMMIM AND URIM BE WITH YOUR PIOUS ONE.  "Now You have given the Tumim and also the Urim to Aharon, who was an important person and the head of the pious tribe, the tribe of Levi."  In this way, he [Moshe] made clear that he [Aharon] was speaking with divine inspiration, with the Divine Presence resting on him, as [the Sages] said, "Every priest who  speaks with divine inspiration, with the Divine Presence resting on him, may be asked to consult the Urim and Tumim."
text.32_Chapter, 7_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) WHOM YOU TESTED AT MASSAH.  At every trial [masah] with which Israel tried God, may He be blessed, as it says (Num. 14:22), "they have tried Me tem times," the tribe of Levi never tried Him, and so the decree regarding the Spies was not decreed against them.
text.32_Chapter, 7_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) CHALLENGED AT THE WATERS OF MERIBAH.  For You eliminated their two heads, i.e., Moshe and Aharon, because of the waters of Meribah.
text.32_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) WHO SAID OF HIS FATHER. In connection with the Calf.
text.32_Chapter, 8_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) HE IGNORED HIS OWN CHILDREN. YOUR PRECEPTS BECAUSE HE KEPT YOUR INSTRUCTION.  He disregarded the lives of his sons in the wilderness in order to keep Your instruction, i.e., the commandment of circumcising the sons, even though many of them died, as [the Sages] said, "[The Israelites other than the Levites did not circumcise their sons] because the northern wind [which provides relief from the health-impairing hot south wind] did not blow."
text.32_Chapter, 8_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) AND THEY KEPT YOUR COVENANT.  As [the Sages] said, "The tribe of Levi did not worship idolatry."  And this was true both in Egypt and in the wilderness.
text.32_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: THEY SHALL TEACH YOUR LAWS TO YA'AKOV.  Because it is an upstanding tribe, bestow on them grace and discernment so that they can instruct in Your laws, as [the Sages] said, "If the rav is like an angel of the Lord of Hosts, people will seek Torah from his mouth."
text.32_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) BLESS, ADONAI, THEIR WEALTH.  Bless their possessions so that a little business will suffice for them, and they will have free time to contemplate and to teach.
text.32_Chapter, 10_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) AND FAVOR HIS UNDERTAKINGS.  Their service in the Temple should be acceptable to You.
text.32_Chapter, 10_Verse, 2_Comment: (3) RISE NO MORE.  So that they [the enemies] cannot rise against them  [the Levites], as Korah and King Uzziah had done.
text.32_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) BLESSED OF GOD IS HIS LAND.  Yosef's portion is land that is naturally blessed.
text.32_Chapter, 12_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) WITH THE BOUNTY OF DEW FROM HEAVEN.  I pray that its blessing will also be with respect to the bounty of [crops] that ripen through the forces of the heavens, of dew, even without rain, AND OF THE  DEEP ... WITH THE BOUNTEOUS YIELD  ETC.
text.32_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: (1) AND THE FAVOR OF THE PRESENCE IN THE BUSH.  And the favor of God, Who appeared in the bush, where He taught the idea of (Ps. 92:15), "I am with him in his distress."  All of these WILL REST ON THE HEAD OF YOSEF, aside from his blessings along with the whole community; they will come on his head from God above, Who blesses without [using] an intermediary.
text.32_Chapter, 15_Verse, 1_Comment: (2) ON THE CROWN OF THE ELECT OF HIS BROTHERS.  For indeed, he merits this, for he had distinction and a royal crown among his brothers, and he comported himself with all of them generously.
